title: Using computed tomography coronary angiography to asses how heart disease begins and changes over time
official: Coronary artery disease initiation or progression in the long-term: the SCOT-HEART evolution study
summary:
Background and study aims
Coronary artery disease affects the blood vessels of the heart and is one of the commonest causes of death worldwide. Despite advances in diagnosis and treatment, we still do not understand why it develops or gets worse in some people and not in others. This study aims to use a scan of the heart (a computed tomography coronary angiogram) to assess the presence and severity of coronary artery disease in people who previously took part in the SCOT-HEART trial. 

Who can participate?
Patients who were part of the SCOT-HEART trial. 

What does the study involve?
Participants will have a computed tomography scan of the heart, complete questionnaires about their health, lifestyle and medications, and have blood and urine samples, an electrocardiogram (a tracing of the electrical activity of the heart), a blood pressure check, an assessment of their physical activity and a breath test that measures carbon monoxide. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Patients are not expected to gain a direct medical benefit from taking part, although occasionally a scan may reveal something that warrants follow-up with their own doctor. The main value of the study is in helping researchers understand what causes coronary artery disease, which may lead to better ways to prevent and treat disease in the future. 

The computed tomography scan uses a low dose of radiation. The contrast dye is generally safe, although a small number of people can have an allergic reaction to it. The blood test may cause brief discomfort or minor bruising. 

Where is the study run from?
The University of Edinburgh (UK).

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
August 2026 until July 2029.

Who is funding the study?
The British Heart Foundation 

Who is the main contact?
loth.scotheartevolution@nhs.scot

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participation in the SCOT-HEART trial
Exclusion criteria:
1. Inability or unwilling to give informed consent
2. Impaired renal function with eGFR of <30 mL/min/1.73m²
3. Known allergy or contraindications to iodinated contrast
4. Patients who are unable to tolerate the supine position
5. Females of child-bearing age who are pregnant or breastfeeding
